newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MALBAK PAYS SHAREHOLDERS A FURTHER 110 CTS.
newsitem.headline: MALBAK PAYS SHAREHOLDERS A FURTHER 110 CTS.

text.p: South African packaging group Malbak Ltd, which recently unbundled and distributed most of its assets to shareholders, said on Wednesday it was disbursing a further 110 cents to shareholders.

It said in a statement that the funds arose from the 238 million rand raised from the sale of Malbak's stake in Haggie Ltd and in ICL Technology Holdings Ltd, together with the dividends earned on investments Malbak has held and not yet paid to shareholders.
Cash was also received from the Malbak share trust from the sale of certain shares held.
The cash distribution will be made around October 20.
Malbak said that using Tuesday's closing share prices for its major assets, Kohler Ltd and U.K-based MY Holdings Plc, the underlying value per Malbak share is 600 cents.
When added to the cash distribution, the value rises to 710 cents a share.
"This is well in excess of the Malbak market price of 670 cents a share," it said.
Malbak had also set aside an additional 25 cents a share for unbundling costs, contingent liabilities and possible claims against warranties.

The firm said that the 600 cents underlying value comprises an attributable value of 410 cents a share for Malbak's interest in Kohler, 149 cents per Malbak share for the MY Holdings stake and 41 cents a share for cash and near cash assets.
"Adding in the further 25 cents per share of cash retained to meet the various costs of unbundling, Malbak's total underlying value amounts to 625 cents a share on the present share prices," it said.
Malbak added that the valuation would help shareholders attach a more appropriate value to their investment.
